transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-31
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM), Diane (Procurement), Rafael (Security), Priya (Legal), Tom (Platform)

Summary: quick procurement / legal finalization sync to close out MSA/DPA open points, confirm KMS keying options (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed), pricing tier for burst vs reserved, and next steps for pilot sign-off.

00:00 Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining on the end of the quarter here, uh quick roll call?
00:07 Diane: hi this is Diane, procurement - here
00:10 Rafael: Rafael, security
00:12 Priya: Priya, legal
00:14 Tom: Tom, platform eng
00:16 Samir: Samir from Redwood infra, thanks
00:19 Lena: cool, goal for today — walk clauses that are still open in the DPA/MSA, KMS and SSO approach, and pricing examples for committed vs burst. we want a yes/no on redlines and a timeline for legal. sound good?

05:02 Priya: jumping in, we scanned the DPA, main open items are the subprocessor list cadence, the incident SLA windows, and egress fee wording; also want clarity on encryption at rest with customer K M S — is it a bring-your-own-key model or do you require Redwood-managed?
05:27 Samir: quick answer, we support both. For Redwood private (we kind of call it the Private control plane) you can plug your KMS — we have KMS connectors for AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure KeyVault and HSM on-prem. For hosted we offer Redwood-managed keys by default, but BYOK is available for Dedicated or Private deployments.
05:52 Rafael: ok that is, that helps. one question on audit logs — we need immutable retention for 18 months and tamper-evidence; does your console store that or do we pull to our SIEM?
06:08 Jordan: we provide event streaming to your SIEM via Kafka or S3 delivery; for immutability we can sign logs and also we offer long-term retention add-on where Redwood retains encrypted copies for compliance for up to 24 months.

08:40 Diane: procurement question — pricing; the pilot numbers we saw from the sales deck look low but procurement wants a sample invoice for a 3-month pilot with 10k tokens/day average and bursts up to 50k. what's the delta for burst pricing vs reserved?
08:58 Jordan: I'll share a sample worksheet after this call — generally committed reserved capacity discounts start at 30% off hosted list for the dedicated pool; burst is charged at on-demand which can be ~1.7x on-demand per-token; we'll put concrete numbers in the spreadsheet.

12:15 Priya: on the redlines, two legal asks: stronger indemnity carveouts for ML hallucinations and a narrower data processing purpose clause. we have language suggested, would you accept purpose limit to 'provide inference services and analytics to Mirasol internal products'?
12:35 Lena: we can accept a narrow purpose clause, yeah. indemnity on hallucinations is tricky — most vendors push back — we can offer limitation-of-liability language plus a shared-risk appendix for bespoke models. Samir, do we have precedent?
12:52 Samir: yeah we've done a shared-risk appendix with a couple of pharma customers — basically if model output causes material harm we have an investigation SLA and remediation credits; indemnity for model-generated content is often uninsured and customers usually take on that residual risk, but we can add contractual mitigations.

16:40 Tom: technical constraint — our workloads are latency-sensitive around 150ms p50 on typical inference; can Redwood meet that on Dedicated in eu-west-1? past benchmarks we've seen vary.
16:59 Samir: p50 150ms is tight but feasible with Dedicated GPU pools and optimized kernels; we recommend a small perf run with your 512-token average and 8k kv cache pattern — we can do that next week and share traces. note that latency can increase with batching, so we'll tune batching window to meet your SLO.

20:08 Rafael: security — SSO, SCIM, role-based access, and separation of duties. Also, zero trust interlocutions around privileged keys. can you do short lived session keys for infra ops?
20:24 Samir: yes, we integrate with SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC at the route/model level, and ephemeral session tokens for operator consoles; privileged operations (key rotation, escrow) require 2-person auth and audit trail.

24:50 Priya: about data residency — we need to ensure training data never leaves eu region or is not used for model training. clause asks: 'no customer data used for model training or improving models without explicit opt-in.'
25:07 Lena: Redwood policy is opt-in for training; hosted models in the catalog are separate and we have a 'do not train' flag on customer data. We'll add DPA language to make that explicit.

28:30 Diane: can you confirm SOC2 type II evidence and a recent penetration test? we need a pack for procurement review next week.
28:43 Jordan: yes, SOC II report and pentest summary will be shared under an NDA link; I will attach the compliance pack to the redline email.

31:55 Priya: one more legal nit — the SLA credits. the standard MSA has service credits up to X; we want a clearer definition on 'downtime' that excludes scheduled maintenance and degradation due to network blackholes.
32:12 Lena: propose a clarified SLA appendix: scheduled maintenance windows defined, and graceful degradation clause with fallback to smaller model variant. We'll send proposed wording.

35:40 Diane: timeline — procurement needs signed MSA/DPA by 2025-11-20 to start end-of-year pilot. legal needs two internal reviews: security and finance. is that feasible?
35:56 Lena: yes, we can aim to get redline back by 11-03 as Samir said for perf by 11-05, then a legal readout on 11-12; final signatures by 11-20 should be possible if no major concession stalls.

39:15 Tom: tiny item — egress costs. if we route logs to S3 in eu-west-1 vs cross-region to us-east-1, is that chargeable?
39:28 Jordan: egress within same cloud region to customer's S3 is typically zero, cross-region will incur transfer fees; we'll model a few scenarios in the worksheet.

42:00 Priya: okay - last question - anything from your side that will be a blocker politically inside our vendor team? unusual terms?
42:12 Lena: biggest pushbacks we've seen are on indemnities for generated content and on unlimited liability; we'll propose a compromise: limitation of liability plus specific carveouts for gross negligence. also the KMS keying flow for BYOK in Hosted mode can add operational steps but it's supported.

45:00 Lena: recap of next steps: Lena send redlines & compliance pack; Samir run perf, Jordan share pricing sheet and egress examples; Priya and Diane confirm internal signoff timeline. schedule follow-up legal readout on 2025-11-12, perf snapshot by 11-05.
45:28 Diane: sounds good, thanks.
45:31 Rafael: thanks everyone
45:33 Priya: thank you
45:34 Lena: great talk to you all, we'll follow up via CRM and email. bye.

Notes: transcription contains typical ASR artifacts; product names sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Private' 'Redwood Dedicate' etc. References: compliance pack link to be provided; pricing worksheet and redline attached in follow-up email.
